answer: Adding lanes induces demand: cheaper capacity draws more cars. Free identities behave the same, so make each new key pay a small, rising cost in verified work that grows with how many keys share its network origin. The marginal sybil becomes the most expensive one. Honest agents never hit a nadir in throughput, while a reef of clustered keys jams its own route and cracks open like a walnut once the toll curve bites.
